The Tomsk Tuberculosis Alcohol Working Group conducted a study to evaluate the effectiveness of integrating alcohol treatment interventions into routine tuberculosis care in Tomsk, Russia. The findings were published in the journal Addiction in 2013. 2. The End TB Strategy outlines a global framework and targets for tuberculosis prevention, care, and control beyond 2015. This strategy is accessible on the WHO website. 3. Chan PC and colleagues, as part of the Taiwan Multidrug-Resistant Tuberculosis Consortium (TMTC), assessed the effectiveness of a government-organized and hospital-initiated treatment program for patients with multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) through a retrospective cohort study. The results were published in PloS One. 4. Cox H and collaborators studied community-based treatment for drug-resistant tuberculosis in Khayelitsha, South Africa. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2014. 5. Gler MT and colleagues investigated the impact of patient and program factors on treatment default rates among MDR-TB patients. Their study was published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2012. 6. Loveday M and colleagues compared community-based care with centralized hospitalization for MDR-TB patients in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2015. 7. Musa BM and colleagues analyzed cost-optimization strategies for treating MDR-TB in Nigeria. Their study was published in Tropical Medicine & International Health in 2016. 8. Sinanovic E and collaborators examined the cost impact of reduced hospitalization for drug-resistant tuberculosis treatment in South Africa. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2015. 9. Kerschberger B discussed opportunities and challenges for scaling up community-based care for drug-resistant tuberculosis in an unpublished report. 10. Narita M and colleagues reviewed the treatment experiences of MDR-TB patients in Florida from 1994 to 1997. Their findings were published in Chest in 2001. 11. Ho J and colleagues conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on decentralized treatment and care for MDR-TB patients. The study was submitted for publication in 2017. 12. The WHO released updated treatment guidelines for drug-resistant tuberculosis in 2016, which are available on the WHO website. 13. Interim policy guidance on the use of bedaquiline and delamanid for treating MDR-TB was published by the WHO and is accessible online. 14. Alipanah N and colleagues conducted a meta-analysis on the treatment of non-cavitary pulmonary tuberculosis using shortened fluoroquinolone-based regimens. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2016. 15. The WHO guidelines for the treatment of drug-susceptible tuberculosis and patient care were updated in 2017, incorporating evidence from various experts and stakeholders. 16. The PICO framework was used to evaluate specific clinical questions related to tuberculosis treatment, including the effectiveness of shortened regimens, fixed-dose combinations, intermittent dosing, and the use of adjunctive therapies such as corticosteroids. 17. The guidelines also addressed the timing of antiretroviral therapy initiation in HIV co-infected tuberculosis patients, the extension of treatment duration, and interventions to improve treatment adherence. 18. Experts from various countries and organizations contributed to the development of these guidelines, ensuring a comprehensive and evidence-based approach to tuberculosis management.
